articles.title: 'Tem um voto de direita que vai aparecer na eleição', diz Tarcísio | G1
articles.standfirst: Declaração ocorreu em Piracicaba (SP) nesta quarta-feira (23). Para o governador, 'sentimento de cansaço' com PT faz ele acreditar na vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) na disputa presidencial.
articles.summary: Para o governador, 'sentimento de cansaço' com PT faz ele acreditar na vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) na disputa presidencial.
articles.body:
O governador de São Paulo e candidato à reeleição, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), disse nesta quarta-feira (23) que existe um "voto de direita" que não está aparecendo nas pesquisas, mas que irá aparecer no dia da eleição. A declaração de Tarcísio ocorreu durante um evento de campanha em Piracicaba (SP).

Segundo o governador, esse voto e um "sentimento de cansaço" com o PT fazem ele acreditar na vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) na disputa presidencial.

"Um exaurimento com o PT, que já não tem mais nada para apresentar para o Brasil, tem um sentimento de cansaço, existe uma exaustão ética, e ela vai se manifestar no dia da eleição. Esse sentimento não vai ser capturado por pesquisa, esse sentimento vai chegar lá na hora da urna, e a gente vai ver. Tem um voto de direita que não está aparecendo, mas que vai aparecer no dia da eleição, por isso estou acreditando muito na vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro", afirmou.

A pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira mostra Tarcísio com 44% das intenções de voto, e Fernando Haddad (PT), com 27% .

Já na última pesquisa Quaest para a disputa presidencial, divulgada na segunda (21), Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro estão empatados no limite da margem de erro no 1º turno , com 37% e 33%, respectivamente.

Tarcísio de Freitas em Piracicaba — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Ainda durante o evento em Piracicaba, Tarcísio defendeu a eleição dos senadores Guilherme Derrite (PP) e André do Prado (PL) em São Paulo.

Na visão do governador, apenas os dois defendem valores que ele acredita e têm chances de ganhar a eleição.

"A gente precisa de senadores que defendam a vida desde a concepção, que defendam a livre iniciativa, a propriedade privada e que defendam os valores que nós acreditamos. Esses candidatos que tenham chances de chegar, de vencer as eleições são Guilherme Derrite e André do Prado."

articles.title: Feminicídio em Capinópolis: Homem é condenado a 48 anos de prisão | G1
articles.standfirst: Helton Martins Sobrinho, de 61 anos, também foi condenado por dano qualificado e violação de domicílio. Em 2025 ele invadiu a casa da ex-companheira e a matou a facadas em Capinópolis, no Triângulo Mineiro.
articles.summary: Helton Martins Sobrinho recebeu pena de 48 anos pelo feminicídio de Lucimar da Silva em Capinópolis após invadir a residência e descumprir medidas judiciais.
articles.body:
Casa em que Lucimar foi morta por Helton Martins, em Capinópolis — Foto: PM/Divulgação

Helton Martins Sobrinho, de 61 anos, foi condenado a 48 anos, um mês e 15 dias de prisão pelo feminicídio da ex-companheira, Lucimar da Silva, de 65 anos, que aconteceu em 2025, em Capinópolis , no Triângulo Mineiro. O julgamento aconteceu no dia 18 de setembro, no Tribunal do Júri da cidade.

Além da pena de reclusão pelo feminicídio, ele foi condenado a sete meses de detenção e dez dias de multa pelos crimes de dano qualificado e violação de domicílio. A sentença estabeleceu regime inicial fechado.

Em nota o advogado Gênio Antônio Vaz, que representa Helton, afirmou que a defesa entende que a pena aplicada foi desproporcional e excessivamente severa em relação às circunstâncias do crime. Ele afirmou ainda que por essa razão, serão pedidos os recursos cabíveis para buscar a fixação de uma pena justa e condizente com os parâmetros legais.

O Conselho de Sentença acolheu as teses apresentadas pelo Ministério Público de Minas Gerais (MPMG) e rejeitou os pedidos da defesa para que fosse reconhecida a semi-imputabilidade de Helton e para que o crime fosse desclassificado, ou seja, a defesa alegou que o condenado tinha sua capacidade de entender o caráter criminoso do que fez ou de controlar suas ações considerada parcialmente reduzida.

Os jurados também reconheceram circunstâncias que agravaram o feminicídio: Lucimar tinha mais de 60 anos, o crime foi cometido com meio cruel e com recurso que dificultou a defesa da vítima. O homicídio ocorreu ainda durante o descumprimento de medidas protetivas de urgência concedidas anteriormente à mulher.

Segundo o MPMG, Helton não aceitava o fim do relacionamento, que durou cerca de nove anos. Movido por ciúmes e sentimento de posse, ele invadiu a casa da ex-companheira e a atacou com uma faca.

O crime aconteceu na residência de Lucimar, no Centro de Capinópolis . Conforme a denúncia, menos de um mês antes do assassinato, Helton havia sido intimado das medidas judiciais que determinavam que ele se afastasse da vítima e não mantivesse contato com ela.

A sentença também determinou o pagamento de R$ 100 mil de reparação mínima por danos morais aos sucessores de Lucimar.

Helton estava preso preventivamente desde o dia seguinte ao crime. Ele foi levado ao Presídio de Canápolis, onde ficou durante o processo.

Após a condenação, a Justiça autorizou a transferência dele para outra unidade prisional de Minas Gerais, preferencialmente para um estabelecimento com estrutura médica e de enfermagem adequada.

Segundo a decisão, Helton tem hipertensão, diabetes e hiperplasia prostática benigna. Ele utiliza uma sonda vesical de demora e faz uso contínuo de diversos medicamentos.

A direção do presídio informou à Justiça que a unidade enfrenta redução no número de policiais penais e superlotação no regime fechado. Também apontou que o estabelecimento não possui equipe médica e de enfermagem em tempo integral capaz de atender às necessidades do preso.

O Ministério Público não se opôs à transferência. A Justiça determinou que Helton seja levado para uma unidade subordinada ao Departamento Penitenciário de Minas Gerais (Depen-MG) que tenha estrutura para o acompanhamento médico necessário.

O g1 questionou a Secretaria de Estado de Justiça e Segurança Pública de Minas Gerais (Sejusp) sobre o local em que o condenado está preso, e foi informado de que ele permanece no Presídio de Capinópolis.

Na época do assassinato, a Polícia Militar informou que Lucimar já havia denunciado Helton por violência psicológica e ciúmes e conseguido uma medida protetiva.

Após matar a ex-companheira, ele fugiu. Segundo a PM, foi encontrado na residência dele com a faca que teria sido usada no crime e uma camisa manchada de sangue. No momento da prisão, ainda tentou se ferir e precisou ser contido pelos policiais.

Aos militares, Helton afirmou que matou Lucimar por ciúmes.

Para o promotor de Justiça Lucas Sanches Tizzo, a condenação representa uma resposta à violência doméstica e familiar.

“A expressiva condenação demonstra que o ciclo de agressões, ameaças e o desrespeito às ordens judiciais de proteção serão combatidos com o máximo rigor legal”, afirmou.

articles.title: Bombeiros resgatam cachorro preso em cano durante chuva forte | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal entrou na tubulação de uma residência durante a chuva e não conseguiu sair. Cachorro foi resgatado sem ferimentos.
articles.summary: Animal entrou na tubulação de uma residência durante a chuva e não conseguiu sair. Cachorro foi resgatado sem ferimentos.
articles.body:
Cachorrinho foi resgatado sem ferimentos — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Um cachorro ficou preso em um cano de escoamento de água durante uma forte chuva na madrugada desta terça-feira (22), em Ivinhema, em Mato Grosso do Sul. O animal entrou na tubulação de uma residência e não conseguiu sair sozinho.

O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar foi acionado para fazer o resgate. Para alcançar o cachorro, os militares precisaram quebrar parte da calçada e acessar a tubulação.

A equipe também utilizou equipamentos adequados para cortar o cano com segurança. O cachorro foi retirado sem ferimentos e entregue ao tutor.

Os bombeiros orientam que, em situações de risco envolvendo animais ou pessoas, a população acione imediatamente o telefone 193.

A recomendação é não tentar fazer o resgate por conta própria, pois improvisos podem causar ferimentos.

articles.title: Why Watching Couples Make Out in Public Can Feel So Personal
articles.summary: Why does PDA bother some people so much? New dating app data and a clinical psychologist unpack the loneliness, jealousy, and empathy behind it.
articles.body:

Admittedly, there are a few reactions people have to seeing others tangled up in a make-out session. Are you the type to say "Aww" to yourself and keep pushing? Do you roll your eyes? Or maybe, for reasons you may not admit, do you suddenly feel a little…sad? It turns out seeing other people bask in their romantic-related happiness evokes a lot of complicated and personal feelings in the innocent bystanders witnessing the whole thing.

According to a survey conducted by the dating app Hily , a twinge of sadness may be more common among Gen Z witnesses in particular. Nearly 1 in 3 Gen Zers say they don't like seeing couples make out in public , compared to fewer than 1 in 5 millennials. And it isn't actually because they think it's "gross" or "inappropriate"—more than half say seeing a couple kiss in public makes them feel straight-up lonely .

So why does someone else's PDA feel so personal?

PDA has always been polarizing. For some, PDA—whether it's holding hands , a kiss on the cheek, or swapping serious spit—is a sweet declaration that you're in deep infatuation and you don't care who knows it. For the pearl clutchers, it's an unbecoming act that's reserved for the privacy of one's home. But for Gen Z, there are a few different things at play.

Clinical psychologist Sabrina Romanoff , PsyD, says this generation has grown up in a culture where so much of what happens in public is performed—and potentially recorded. In an age of influencers and virality, it can be hard to imagine anything done in public without wondering about the motive behind it. "In some ways, PDA can feel performative," she says.

Beyond that, though, Gen Z has had some pretty intense stats: The New York Times has said they're having the least sex , the fewest romantic relationships , according to the Survey Center on American Life, and are being called the " loneliest generation ."

Which brings us back to how deeply personal it could feel to watch someone else make out. If seeing someone else's intimacy makes you feel bad, it may be less about the couple in front of you and more about what their intimacy brings up in you.

"PDA is shining a light on what we don't have in such an explicit, tangible, almost primitive way," Romanoff says. "A lot of people tend to project their own insecurities onto PDA."

This spark of jealousy doesn't necessarily mean that you want what that particular couple has. It can simply point to something you wish you had more of in your own life. As Romanoff puts it, that feeling can be a signal of an area of your life you want to "feel more full in" or "put more effort into."

The problem is what happens when we don't stop to figure out what the feeling is trying to tell us. "Instead, when people are triggered with a bad emotion…it's very easy to just turn on the person whi triggered you," Romanoff says.

Think about the Central Park bench incident . In July, a TikToker posted a video of two adult strangers kissing on a bench as he shouted, "Get a room! There's kids around." The video now has more than 4 million views. The people's identities have been revealed, along with details about their workplace and families. But why the urge to record them?

There is much to be said about the surveillance state we're all living in and the increasingly blurred lines between witnessing something in public and making content out of it. But Romanoff also points to the emotional impulse behind recording strangers and shaming them.

"If we aren't willing to say, 'Wait, maybe this is speaking to something that I have unresolved in me,' it's very easy to just project it out there and say the problem is there," she says.

What do you do if you recognize this feeling in yourself?

For starters, don't act on the emotion as it comes up. Romanoff recommends stopping to observe what's happening internally before deciding what to do with it. A big reaction, she says, can be an indicator that something else underlying has been activated.

"That's a signal for you to take a step back and take inventory. Okay, what's being activated in me? What wound is being reopened here? "

That doesn't mean you need to turn every make-out session you witness into a deep psychological analysis. Sometimes you're simply annoyed. But if the feeling is bigger than the situation seems to warrant, it may be worth asking yourself what exactly you're reacting to.

As Romanoff puts it: "People make the mistake of having a big emotion and then following the action urge that comes with that emotion."

And more than anything, people make the mistake of forgetting that that couple on the bench is also human—and that perhaps there was a time when you were so enamored with another person that you would French kiss them in broad daylight in a public park and not care who was around to see.

The idea that we should shame PDA ultimately means losing more than just people making out on the street. "The biggest thing that we are losing is our empathy for people," Romanoff says.

No one says you have to enjoy watching strangers make out. But maybe you don't need to hate it either.

articles.title: The 9 best pumpkin spice products you can buy in the supermarket, according to chefs
articles.summary: Don't limit yourself to coffee — there are tasty fall treats in every aisle, starting at just $3.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

The air feels crisp, the leaves are starting to turn and you can finally bundle up in your favorite sweater s — yep, it's officially fall. And in my humble opinion, one major plus of the seasonal shift is the reintroduction of pumpkin spice everything. Beyond those Pumpkin Spice Lattes from Starbucks, you'll find fall-flavored yogurt, popcorn, granola, cookies, protein bars and more. (There are even pumpkin-spiced treats for your dog !)

Of course, some of these snacks are better than others, and while I've tried a lot of them, I turned to professional chefs with impeccable palates to hear about their favorites. Yes, even chefs like pumpkin spice! Here are nine supermarket finds they say are worth adding to your shopping cart.

This pumpkin pie flavor comes with a pumpkin cookie crumble that makes the high-protein cup (12 grams to be exact!) taste more like dessert. "For pumpkin spice yogurts, the Seattle original Elleno's Pumpkin Pie yogurt is where it's at," says Megan Keno, food blogger and the author of Cast Iron Gourmet . "It's not overly sweet, and it has the tang of a high-quality Greek yogurt. The pumpkin crunchy toppings just seal the deal."

Of course, Starbucks created the PSL, but if you prefer to make your coffee at home , you can trust its creamer to help you get the same flavor. It's even chef-approved! "It's very convenient and works amazingly well with a stronger coffee because the cinnamon, nutmeg and pumpkin flavors come out well without needing those extra syrups," says Ribe Rubio, a private chef with Platesfull .

If you enjoy a sweet cinnamon raisin bagel, we'll assume you're down for a similarly sweet topping like this pumpkin spice cream cheese. "This is versatile and works well on a toasted bagel or English muffin, but one can also use it on dessert dishes," Rubio says.

Before its yearly advent calendar sells out, fans go wild for another Bonne Maman seasonal offering. "Limited, but worth the hunt, is Bonne Maman's Pumpkin Spice Spread," says Keno. "Putting this on just basic toast in the morning with coffee is a fall-coded way to start the day. It's got all the warm fall spices with cinnamon, nutmeg and clove but isn't cloyingly sweet."

This is another one of Rubio's favorites. (FYI, it's just pancake mix, but made with gluten-free oats.) Just add water, mix, pour and cook to make yourself a tasty, heaping stack. Rubio describes the pumpkin spice flavor as "very subtle and natural" and says it "gives you the fall flavor without being overly sweet."

If you don't want to use creamer in your coffee to get the pumpkin spice flavor, try this simple syrup. It's "a great way to bring those seasonal pumpkin and warm spice flavors into coffee or lattes at home," says Kit Skarstrom, executive chef at Conrad New York Downtown in NYC. "The addition of butternut squash gives it a little more nuance than a traditional pumpkin spice syrup, while still delivering those familiar fall flavors people look forward to this time of year." (It's also great in cocktails or as a sweetener in desserts.)

Been to a Trader Joe's lately? The store has reached expert level when it comes to its pumpkin spice fall treats. Katherine Sprung , pastry chef and founder of NYC's Squish Marshmallows, recommends its yogurt-coated pumpkin spice pretzels. "I love yogurt pretzels, and these just give that extra-cozy feeling of fall, my favorite season! I also love anything salty-sweet, so it's really a great combo."

The chefs I spoke with raved about this TJ's treat. While it's called a sheet cake, it's a miniature one — it serves 4-6 people. But hey, no shame if you want to get one just for yourself and enjoy a slice with your PSLs in the afternoons.

"If you need a pre-baked pumpkin spice treat, the only one you need is Trader Joe's Pumpkin Spice Mini Sheet Cake," says Keno. "Just don't even bother elsewhere. It's moist and has a thick layer of cream cheese frosting on top. It's my guilty pleasure when I don't want to bake for myself."

Rubio adds that "the warm spices [are] noticeable but not overpowering."

Plenty of the chefs I spoke with said they make their own pumpkin spice treats using real pumpkin. " Libby's pumpkin purée with a good spice blend beats anything pre-flavored on the shelf, but if we're talking ready-made, King Arthur Pumpkin Spice Blend is the one I keep stocked," says Daniel P. Craig, chef and founder of Kitchen Deets .

This mix of cinnamon, ginger, clove, allspice and nutmeg doesn't contain sugar or artificial sweeteners. "Most grocery-store pumpkin spice products bury the pumpkin under sugar; this one respects the spice itself and lets me build sweetness separately," Craig adds.

articles.title: In 2017, one woman began collecting menstrual products for women in need; 8 years later, Project Dignity was supporting nearly 1,900 women and girls every month
articles.summary: For many women, buying pads or tampons is an ordinary part of the monthly shop.
articles.body: For many women, buying pads or tampons is an ordinary part of the monthly shop. For someone already struggling to pay for food, rent or other essentials, the same purchase can become a difficult calculation. Across Western North Carolina, that gap has left some women and girls without reliable access to menstrual products. The consequences can reach into school, work and everyday routines. According to Deerfield Charitable Foundation, in Hendersonville, Barbara Morgan began responding to that problem in 2017 by collecting menstrual supplies for people who could not afford them. What started as a small local effort has since developed into Project Dignity, a nonprofit whose volunteers now help nearly 1,900 women and girls each month.How Morgan’s menstrual support effort expanded over eight yearsProject Dignity began in 2017, when Morgan started gathering menstrual products for women who needed them. At the time, the work was a grassroots effort rather than a large distribution operation, with volunteers and donation boxes helping collect supplies.The need was tied to a basic household expense that can be difficult to absorb when money is already tight. Food assistance does not cover menstrual products, leaving some women to decide how to stretch limited resources from one part of the month to the next.Morgan's project focused on filling that particular gap. Pads and tampons were collected and then made available to women and girls who otherwise might go without them. Eight years later, the scale of the work looks very different.Project Dignity now reaches nearly 1,900 women and girls each monthProject Dignity has expanded from its original community effort into a nonprofit serving people across ten counties in Western North Carolina. Nearly 1,900 women and girls receive monthly menstrual supplies through the organisation.As reported by the foundation, its distribution network includes more than 148 schools and 59 social service agencies. That means the products are reaching people through places already connected to students, families and individuals seeking other forms of support.The expansion also shows how the project has moved beyond simply collecting donations. Volunteers now take part in a continuing supply and distribution operation, helping prepare menstrual products for people who need them month after month.For those relying on the service, the practical value is straightforward. The products are available without having to be bought from an already limited household budget.Schools became an important part of the distribution networkStudents are among the people supported through Project Dignity's work. Menstrual products can be a small part of a school's supplies, but not having them when they are needed can interfere with a student's ability to remain in class.Project Dignity distributes supplies through more than 148 schools, extending its reach into communities where young people may otherwise have limited access to free menstrual products.The organisation also works with social service agencies. There are 59 such agencies within its distribution network, connecting the project with people facing different circumstances, including women living in low-income housing and victims of domestic violence.The project also works beyond schoolsProject Dignity's reach includes women who may not have any connection to a school-based programme. Social service agencies provide another route for distributing the monthly supplies, allowing the organisation to reach adults as well as younger people. The project identifies period poverty as affecting people who cannot consistently afford menstrual products. In households where money is being divided between food and other necessities, pads and tampons can become an expense that is pushed aside.That can have practical effects. Without adequate supplies, some women and girls may miss school or work, while others may experience discomfort or health concerns. The problem is not limited to the cost of one packet of products. It recurs every month.Volunteers turned collection boxes into a continuing operationVolunteer involvement has remained part of the project since its early days. What began with a small number of people collecting donations has developed into regular packing and distribution work. That work includes preparing menstrual products for delivery to schools and social service agencies. Donation drives provide the materials, while volunteers help turn those donations into individual supplies that can be distributed to people who need them.The process can look ordinary from the outside: boxes of products being collected, sorted and packed. Yet the organisation's monthly figures depend on that routine being repeated. Nearly 1,900 women and girls now receive support each month, making the volunteer effort an ongoing part of Project Dignity's operation rather than a one-off community campaign.How local volunteers help prepare menstrual hygiene kits for studentsThe organisation's work has also been supported through local volunteer events. One such event was planned at Deerfield, where residents were invited to take part in a Project Dignity packing party.The session was scheduled for August 8 2025, at 10am in the Blue Ridge Room. Volunteers were asked to assemble feminine hygiene kits intended to help students begin the school year with the supplies they needed. The products are gathered, turned into kits and prepared for distribution through Project Dignity's existing network. For an organisation serving thousands of people over the course of a year, those individual volunteer sessions become part of a much larger chain of work.Eight years changed the scale of Morgan's original ideaThe distance between Morgan's first collection effort in 2017 and Project Dignity's current reach is measured not only in the number of people served, but also in the infrastructure built around the project. The organisation now operates across ten counties, works through more than 148 schools and 59 social service agencies, and provides monthly supplies to nearly 1,900 women and girls.The underlying task, though, remains familiar. Menstrual products have to be collected, packed and delivered to people who cannot reliably afford them. What began with one woman collecting supplies in Hendersonville has grown into a recurring community service, supported by donations and volunteers and focused on an expense that many households have to meet every month.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Lian Yunzhi, 6-year-old Chinese girl who broke women’s Rubik’s Cube world record twice in 3 days; solved in 4.27 seconds
articles.summary: A six-year-old girl from China has stunned the speedcubing world after breaking the women's 3x3 Rubik's Cube average world record twice within three days,
articles.body: A six-year-old girl from China has stunned the speedcubing world after breaking the women's 3x3 Rubik's Cube average world record twice within three days, becoming the first female speedcuber to record an average time of less than 4.5 seconds.Lian Yunzhi, from Chengdu in China's Sichuan province, first set the women's record with an average solve time of 4.52 seconds at a World Cube Association-certified competition in Wuhan. Three days later, she lowered her own mark to 4.27 seconds at another WCA-certified competition in Guangzhou.The average was calculated from five attempts, with Lian completing the individual solves in times that included a remarkable 4.02 seconds. Her new 4.27-second average made her the only female speedcuber in the world to have officially averaged below 4.5 seconds, according to reports citing Chinese state media.Lian, who is nicknamed "Zhizhi", was introduced to the Rubik's Cube through a class when she was younger. Her mother, Lin Yangxi, told local media that she initially enrolled her daughter in the activity along with other extracurricular classes, including dance and music.The family eventually focused more heavily on cubing after Lin noticed her daughter's aptitude for it.According to her mother, Lian has mastered more than 1,300 Rubik's Cube-solving algorithms and trains for around two to three hours every day. Her parents also took her to Shanghai to train with professional coaches, with her performance improving significantly afterward.Footage released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV shows Lian wearing a red gingham bow while rapidly turning the cube. After completing a solve, she places the cube on the table, claps her hands and pumps her fist in celebration.Her mother said solving the cube can help children develop concentration, memory, logical thinking and spatial awareness. She also stressed that speedcubing involves more than memorising formulas, saying logical reasoning is required to find efficient solutions.The overall 3x3 Rubik's Cube single-solve world record is currently held by nine-year-old Polish speedcuber Teodor Zajder, who solved the puzzle in 2.76 seconds earlier this year.You use AI every day. articles.title: Since the 1923 flooding created Wisconsin’s Chippewa Flowage, floating bogs have drifted across the lake; today, boaters push a 40-acre forest away from the only bridge
articles.summary: Discover the unique story of Wisconsin's Chippewa Flowage and the challenge of moving a 40-acre floating forest that threatens to block the only bridge connecting the lake's east and west sides. Join local boaters in their efforts to navigate this ecological phenomenon.
articles.body: On the Chippewa Flowage in northern Wisconsin, there is a 40-acre patch of forest that has no fixed address. It drifts across the lake's western side on its own schedule and when the wind is wrong, it drifts straight toward the only bridge connecting the flowage's east and west sides. When that happens, there is really only one practical option locals have found: boat owners gather, sometimes twenty of them, sometimes fifty, and use their bows to push the floating forest out of the way. Since the lake's formation, the people here have had to cope with these floating bogs, and nothing suggests the problem is resolving itself. It cannot be divided into pieces and then cleaned up since it is considered an ecological zone that shelters its own plant and animal species. The people only have one choice: to move it around for a bit.A 1923 flood project turned buried swampland into open waterChippewa Flowage, also called Lake Chippewa, is a lake that is 15,300 acres and is located in Sawyer County, Wisconsin. It is 15 miles east of Hayward. The Chippewa Flowage was formed in 1923 due to the flooding of a large swamp area caused by the Winter Dam for hydropower production, according to the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources. It's the third-largest lake in Wisconsin, with an irregularly shaped, mostly undeveloped shoreline stretching 233 miles and encompassing over 200 undeveloped islands, per the Chippewa Flowage Joint Agency Management Plan.Submerged peat bogs rose to the surface after the floodingAs the years went by, organic matter submerged by the flooding gradually rose to the surface, providing a base for plants and creating floating bogs. The anaerobic breakdown of the plant material results in the formation of gases like methane and carbon dioxide, which make it buoyant. This is a phenomenon that has been well documented to occur in peat bogs all over the world. Local stories indicate that this phenomenon could also be responsible for the floating bogs observed in the Chippewa Flowage following the flood of 1923. Within the next few years, with the help of the winds and birds, seeds started growing on these new floating islands of peat, soil, and roots, creating grass and trees on these floating pieces of land.The Forty Acre Bog grew mature tamarack trees on the lake's west sideThese floating bogs vary greatly in their sizes; some are not more than the size of a car park, while others cover several acres. The Forty-Acre Bog, which is one of the most extensive and well-known floating bogs of the Chippewa Flowage, exists on the western part of the reservoir.Over the years, this bog has grown into a community of tamarack trees, whose branches catch the wind and set the whole bog adrift. According to the locals, the tamarack trees behave just like sails in that the wind moves the entire bog, covering several miles over the lake's surface.The bog regularly drifts toward the flowage's only bridgeThat's largely a matter of geography. A bridge crosses the flowage, connecting its eastern and western shores, and it sits directly in the path the Forty Acre Bog tends to follow. When wind and currents shift, they push the bog toward the bridge, and left alone, it would eventually block the crossing entirely.Dozens of boat owners push the bog back into open waterIf the bog moves near the bridge, there is a tradition of local boaters congregating to help push the bog back out into the open water, as noted in the local lore of the area and the history of the resort. Reports of the effort involve anywhere from 20 to 50 boats nudging the bog back into the lake with synchronized surges that might even use walkie-talkies for coordination, and at a speed of much less than a mile per hour. It takes many hours to do this, and a strong wind gust could undo all the hard work in just seconds, turning the bog 30 degrees or more off its course. Since the bog is considered a wildlife habitat and is therefore protected, there is nothing else to do but move it aside.A history of bogs that eventually break apart on their ownNot all bogs on the flowage last as long as Forty Acre Bog has. The locals remember how a huge bog near Deerfoot Lodge had existed for years, until water and wind eventually tore it into pieces and spread them over the lake. Even though this event left an impression on people’s minds, it did not get officially recorded by the state. New bogs may be formed even after the flood of 1923, since new parts of organic matter continue to be released from the lake bed. For now, however, Forty Acre Bog remains the most stubborn and most disturbing resident of the flowage, which is a fully grown forest without any roots in the ground at all.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress Wednesday led the opposition in demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar be sacked and an SC-monitored probe be ordered into the "rot", amid reports that two ECs repeatedly opposed various steps taken about SIR.The opposition announced it will move "impeachment motions" against Kumar whenever a "special session" of Parliament is called. Then what did the CEC do about these objections? In the first three phases of SIR, 13.8 crore names were removed from draft electoral rolls of 31 states and UTs."Party general secretary K C Venugopal said, "How the hell can one man, acting on his master's orders, strike off names at whim? How can he sideline fellow constitutional officers to take blatantly illegal steps that put our democracy in danger?"Singhvi said the revelations are an example of a "double bulldozer sarkar". He said SC has clearly ruled that all election commissioners, including the CEC, function on equal footing, and the revelations about the watchdog's functioning show that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who dissented against the CEC were in a majority.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: New York Islanders set to unleash culinary 'disasterpiece' on unsuspecting fans this season
articles.summary: The New York Islanders unveiled a Nerds Gummy Clusters grilled cheese sandwich, and the bizarre arena concession item is turning heads and stomachs.
articles.body: Most of us are taught at a pretty young age that just because you like two separate things doesn't mean combining them makes an awesome new entity. For example, you may love your wife while also being a big fan of grabbing some drinks with your college boys, but combining the two is probably not the best idea in the world. This applies to food too, as you wouldn't catch me combining pickles with a chocolate milkshake, despite my love for both. VEGAS GOLDEN KNIGHTS BUST OUT THE CONCESSION STAND BIG GUNS FOR STANLEY CUP FINAL Why, then, on God's green earth, did the New York Islanders think it would be a swell idea to put Nerds Gummy Clusters in grilled cheese and call it an edible concession item? Someone get me a bucket! I like grilled cheese. I'm also a big fan of Nerds Gummy Clusters. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! But maybe we should keep these two things on separate ends of the meal spectrum, where they belong. What is it with sports arenas and combining the most bizarrely incompatible food items they can think of? It's almost as if we are in some sort of culinary arms race, and all these teams are trying to outdo one another to try and drum up some press clippings (which I'm clearly contributing to). My mom always told me not to knock something until I try it, but I think I'll skip the Nerds grilled cheese abomination and just assume I'm not a fan. The sad thing is that there has to be a market for these Frankenstein-esque creations, otherwise these arenas would stop making them altogether. If you're reading this and you happen to be one of the sickos that would willingly try something like a Nerds grilled cheese sandwich, do me a favor: don't. I'd like to be able to go more than a month or two without seeing the worst menu item on the face of the planet and then getting worked up into a frenzy having to write about it. The beautiful thing about capitalism is we can make this stuff go away by just not buying it. So the next time you're at an Islanders game, maybe opt for the plastic hockey stick filled with beer or some nachos out of a goalie mask. articles.title: California gunman repeatedly released before deadly rampage, fiery shootout with deputies
articles.summary: Derek Spencer was arrested three times and released in Sacramento County in the weeks before he allegedly gunned down Cheryl Macy in Placer County.
articles.body: A California murder suspect was arrested three times in less than two weeks and walked out of jail after each bust before authorities said his crime spree ended with an innocent woman dead and a fiery shootout with deputies. Prosecutors said they tried to keep Derek Spencer, 44, behind bars after he allegedly assaulted a Sacramento County sheriff’s deputy. Instead, he posted bail, was arrested twice more and was released both times before allegedly killing 76-year-old Cheryl Macy, a beloved former Placer County District Attorney’s Office employee. "Sadly, this should never have occurred but bail reform in California has prioritized criminal offenders over victims," the Sacramento County District Attorney’s Office said in a statement to Fox News Digital. Spencer was ultimately killed early Monday after allegedly opening fire on Placer County sheriff’s deputies during a tense standoff in the rugged forest near Iowa Hill. MANHUNT UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA AFTER ARMED SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY POINTS GUN AT PEOPLE, SHOOTS AT OFFICERS Authorities said he also set two fires as tactical teams closed in, forcing an overnight helicopter rescue of three SWAT operators threatened by the flames. VIDEO SHOWS POLICE TAKE DOWN COP KILLER WITH ARMORED VEHICLE AFTER GUNMAN TURNED NEIGHBORHOOD INTO WAR ZONE The deadly chain of events followed a string of arrests and releases that prosecutors said exposed dangerous gaps in California’s bail system. The first arrest came Sept. 3, when Sacramento County deputies accused Spencer of felony vandalism, resisting arrest and assaulting a deputy with a deadly weapon. CHARLOTTE REPEAT OFFENDER CHARGED WITH KILLING MAN HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON BOND The Sacramento County DA’s office filed charges Sept. 8, including felony assault with a deadly weapon likely to cause great bodily injury and attempting, through threats and violence, to prevent the deputy from carrying out official duties. Prosecutors asked that Spencer remain in custody, but a judge set bail as required by law, the DA’s office said. Spencer posted it and was released Sept. 11. REPEAT OFFENDER BUSTED AGAIN LESS THAN 24 HOURS AFTER RELEASE IN BRAZEN JEWELRY STORE THEFT CASE: POLICE Then the arrests kept coming. At about 11 p.m. Sept. 13, Folsom police responded to an alarm at a model home in the 4600 block of Dehone Circle. Officers encountered Spencer walking out of the property and arrested him on suspicion of burglary, the department told Fox News Digital. ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH BRUTAL SLAYING ONE DAY AFTER CALIFORNIA JUDGE RELEASED HIM: DHS He was booked into the Sacramento County Main Jail and released on his own recognizance the following day, prosecutors said. Two days later, Sacramento County deputies arrested Spencer again, this time on suspicion of stealing a vehicle. He posted bail and was back out of custody Sept. 17. HOW A NONCITIZEN SUSPECTED KILLER GOT CAUGHT AND RELEASED BY NEWSOM-APPOINTED JUDGE: TIMELINE By then, Spencer was also due in court for a preliminary hearing in the deputy-assault case. He failed to appear Sept. 18, prompting a judge to issue a warrant, according to the DA’s office. Prosecutors were still reviewing the burglary and vehicle-theft reports for possible charges when Spencer’s alleged rampage moved into neighboring counties. Authorities said Spencer stole another vehicle and guns and fired at a moving vehicle in El Dorado County on Sept. 19. The next day, Placer County deputies began hunting for him after he allegedly pointed a gun at victims. Deputies spotted Spencer in the Iowa Hill area, but he allegedly rammed a sheriff’s patrol vehicle and escaped. Authorities said he later fired at deputies and law enforcement helicopters, triggering an intensive manhunt and warnings for residents to lock their doors and stay inside. As tactical teams cleared a home where Spencer had been seen, they found Macy shot to death inside. Investigators believe Spencer killed her before fleeing into the surrounding forest. Authorities have not publicly identified any prior connection between the two. REMAINING SUSPECT IN TUCSON POLICE CADET KILLING CAPTURED AFTER FIVE-DAY MANHUNT A California Highway Patrol aircraft using infrared technology located Spencer shortly before 2:30 a.m. Monday, according to the Placer County Sheriff’s Office. Several tactical teams spent hours moving through the steep, heavily wooded terrain in darkness to reach him. When deputies approached, Spencer opened fire, authorities said. A standoff followed, and drone video allegedly captured him starting two separate fires. At about 4 a.m., Spencer fired again from behind a berm, prompting deputies to return fire and fatally strike him, the sheriff’s office said. The flames soon threatened SWAT operators in the forest. A tactical flight crew from the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office RAVEN aviation unit flew through darkness and low-visibility conditions to hoist three operators out of the area. The unit said the mission relied on a specialized night-hoist capability available to only a limited number of law enforcement aviation teams in the region. The Placer County Sheriff’s Office called the case a "dangerous crime spree that took a tragic turn, resulting in the loss of an innocent life." The Sacramento County DA’s office pointed to the California Supreme Court’s recent Kowalczyk decision, arguing that it has limited judges’ ability to detain repeat offenders before trial, even when they may pose a danger. "While the District Attorney’s Office has and will continue to argue that dangerous and repeat offenders like Derek Spencer remain in custody, California must repeal the Kowalczyk decision and change the law to prioritize victims when addressing bail," the office said. The Placer County DA’s office separately said Spencer’s repeated releases raised "serious questions" about whether state law and recent court decisions give judges enough power to prevent similar tragedies. "As prosecutors, our responsibility is not only to seek justice after someone is harmed, but to speak plainly when the system presents warning signs that cannot be ignored," the office said. Macy served the Placer County DA’s office from 2006 to 2020 and remained a cherished part of its extended family. She was also a mother, grandmother and great-grandmother. Placer County District Attorney Morgan Gire honored Macy at a county Board of Supervisors meeting Wednesday, telling community leaders that her death had left his office and the wider community heartbroken. BAKERSFIELD, CALIFORNIA HOSTAGE STANDOFF ENDS AFTER FBI KILLS ARMED SEX OFFENDER Gire called for answers, transparency and accountability while urging the community to remember how Macy lived rather than how she died. His office said former colleagues remembered the energy she brought to her work, the warmth she showed others and the lasting impact she made across Placer County. "The loss of Cheryl is devastating to our office and to the entire community," the office said. "Our hearts are with her family, her friends, and everyone who knew and loved her." Her granddaughter, Addison, told KCRA that Macy had a special way of hugging her loved ones: three squeezes to say, "I love you." "She was the only person who’s ever done that and told me that," Addison said, calling it a memory she will always carry. articles.title: EC faultlines have a long history, dating back to 1989
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that faultlines within the Election Commission are out in the open.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that faultlines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989, reports Bharti Jain.Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in Oct 1989 and joined EC then led by chief election commissioner (CEC) R V S Peri Sastri. It is widely believed the new arrangement was perceived by Shastri as a dilution in power. By Jan 1990, their appointments were rescinded, and EC reverted to being a single-member body.In 1993, with T N Seshan as an all-powerful CEC, the commission was once again made a multi-member body with appointment of ECs M S Gill and G V G Krishnamurthy. What followed was a running feud between Seshan on the one hand and Gill and Krishnamurthy on the other. It was on Seshan's plea challenging govt's decision to make EC a multi-member body that the SC had, in 1995, ruled that the election commissioners and CEC were equal in status, power, and decision-making authority and that CEC was only "first among equals".The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla between 2006 and 2009. Months before he was to step down, Gopalaswami wrote to the President recommending the removal of Chawla for a pro-Congress bias.Differences cropped up between then CEC Sunil Arora and then EC Ashok Lavasa, both appointees of Modi govt, during the 2019 LS polls. Lavasa resigned on Aug 18, 2020, two years short of his tenure.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Alabama has turned a decommissioned natural gas rig into two artificial reefs; one section rises 632 feet from the seafloor, preserving marine habitat that has been growing there since 1998
articles.summary: Far below Alabama’s Gulf Coast, a structure that once belonged to the energy industry is beginning a second life beneath the waves.
articles.body: Far below Alabama’s Gulf Coast, a structure that once belonged to the energy industry is beginning a second life beneath the waves. The decommissioned Spirit VK 780A natural gas rig, located offshore, has been transformed into two artificial reef sites, allowing its massive steel framework to remain part of the marine environment rather than being removed entirely, states an online report by the Outdoor Alabama website. The project adds two new sites to Alabama’s extensive artificial reef network and preserves a marine habitat that has been developing around the rig for decades.From gas platform to underwater habitatThe Spirit VK 780A was located roughly 60 nautical miles south of the Sand Island Lighthouse before being repurposed through an agreement between its former owner, APA Corporation, and the Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, states the report. The project is part of Alabama’s Rigs to Reefs program, which allows decommissioned oil and natural gas structures to be donated to the state’s artificial reef system.For the Spirit VK 780A project, APA Corporation also provided $1.5 million to the Marine Resources Division. The funding supports research, monitoring, habitat restoration and management of Alabama’s marine resources.Rather than removing the entire structure, crews took the platform portion ashore for decommissioning. The remaining legs and well jacket were cut 90 feet below the water’s surface, creating a navigable reef area around the base while retaining the substantial underwater portions of the structure.Two reefs, two very different profilesAccording to the report, the upper section, designated VK 780-T, is now an artificial reef in 206 feet of water within the Tatum Winn South reef zone. Measuring 85 by 77 feet, the rectangular structure extends 107 feet upward from the seafloor.The much larger base, VK 780-B, remains in 722 feet of water. Its enormous framework rises 632 feet from the seafloor, making it a particularly substantial addition to Alabama’s offshore reef system.More importantly, the base retains habitat that has been developing around the platform since 1998. Marine organisms that established themselves on the structure now have a chance to remain part of the Gulf ecosystem.A reef designed to last for decadesArtificial reefs created from retired oil and gas structures can provide stable marine habitat for more than 50 years. Their steel surfaces offer places for corals and other organisms to attach, while the complex framework creates shelter and feeding areas for fish and other marine species. Alabama has been building on that model for decades. The Marine Resources Division established the Marathon Reef and Swingle Reef from retired rigs in 1983, and both remain productive reef sites more than 40 years later, states the report.The Spirit VK 780A now joins that long-running experiment in giving industrial structures a lasting role beneath the Gulf. What was once infrastructure for extracting natural gas has become part of an underwater landscape, one designed to support marine life long after its original purpose ended.Image Courtesy: Outdoor AlabamaYou use AI every day.
